    <ecd:CompActuallyPaidVsTotalShareholderRtnTextBlock contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_30_2023" id="ixv-20500"> &lt;div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: arial;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;"&gt;Relationship Between Compensation Actually Paid and our Total Shareholder Return &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt; &lt;div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"&gt;Our stock price performance is the predominant factor that determines whether the Compensation Actually Paid to our named executive officers is at, above, or below the amounts reported in our summary compensation tables. The Compensation Actually Paid directly correlates with our total shareholder return (&#x201c;TSR&#x201d;) since most of our executive compensation is delivered through long-term equity awards in the form of PRSUs, RSUs, and stock options which vary in value with changes to our stock price.     <ecd:CompActuallyPaidVsNetIncomeTextBlock contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_30_2023" id="ixv-20567"> &lt;div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: arial;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;"&gt;Relationship Between Compensation Actually Paid and our Net Income (GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;Non-GAAP)&lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt; &lt;div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"&gt;GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income are key measures of our overall profitability and can contribute to changes in our stock price, which in turn primarily drives Compensation Actually Paid. We do not use GAAP net income as a financial measure in our executive compensation program, but we use &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income which is derived from our GAAP net income. &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;Non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income is the primary performance factor for determining cash bonuses under our EIP for each of the covered fiscal years and the growth of our &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; earnings per share, which is derived from our &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income, is also a performance measure used to determine the payouts under the annual PRSU awards granted in each of the covered fiscal years. &lt;/div&gt; &lt;div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"&gt;Between 2020 and 2021, our GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income increased and there was a slight increase in CEO Compensation Actually Paid but a slight decrease in Average Compensation Actually Paid to &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;Non-CEO&lt;/div&gt; Named Executive Officers. In 2022, GAAP net income and the Compensation Actually Paid decreased while &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income increased. In 2023, our GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income declined as compared to 2022 but there was an increase in Compensation Actually Paid. The decline in 2023 GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income are not directly correlated to Compensation Actually Paid in 2023 because Compensation Actually Paid was largely driven by the increase to our stock price as illustrated above. &lt;/div&gt; </ecd:CompActuallyPaidVsNetIncomeTextBlock>
    <ecd:CompActuallyPaidVsCoSelectedMeasureTextBlock contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_30_2023" id="ixv-20568"> &lt;div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: arial;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;"&gt;Relationship Between Compensation Actually Paid and our Net Income (GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;Non-GAAP)&lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt; &lt;div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"&gt;GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income are key measures of our overall profitability and can contribute to changes in our stock price, which in turn primarily drives Compensation Actually Paid. We do not use GAAP net income as a financial measure in our executive compensation program, but we use &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income which is derived from our GAAP net income. &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;Non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income is the primary performance factor for determining cash bonuses under our EIP for each of the covered fiscal years and the growth of our &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; earnings per share, which is derived from our &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income, is also a performance measure used to determine the payouts under the annual PRSU awards granted in each of the covered fiscal years. &lt;/div&gt; &lt;div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:8%; font-size:10pt; font-family:arial"&gt;Between 2020 and 2021, our GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income increased and there was a slight increase in CEO Compensation Actually Paid but a slight decrease in Average Compensation Actually Paid to &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;Non-CEO&lt;/div&gt; Named Executive Officers. In 2022, GAAP net income and the Compensation Actually Paid decreased while &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income increased. In 2023, our GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income declined as compared to 2022 but there was an increase in Compensation Actually Paid. The decline in 2023 GAAP and &lt;div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;;display:inline;"&gt;non-GAAP&lt;/div&gt; net income are not directly correlated to Compensation Actually Paid in 2023 because Compensation Actually Paid was largely driven by the increase to our stock price as illustrated above. &lt;/div&gt; </ecd:CompActuallyPaidVsCoSelectedMeasureTextBlock>
